textbookText: 10. Exoskeleton is made up of either chitin (in perisarc) or cacium carbonate (in corals). 11. There is a internal hollow cavity inside the body called gastrovascular cavity or

coelenteron which is lined by gastrodermis. This cavity opens anteriorly by an opening called mouth and ends blindly at the posterior side. 12. They are carnivorous animal. Digestion is both extracellular and intracellular. 13. Respiratory, circulatory, excretory systems are absent. Respiration takes place through general body surface. 14. They have radial or biradial symmetry about a longitudinal oral-aboral axis. 15. They have primitive and diffused type of nervous system in which nerve cells form a network called nerve net on either side of mesogloea in epidermis and gastrodermis but no central nervous system in them. 16. Sensory organs are ocelli (light receptor); statocyst (maintaining orientation) in free swimming forms. 17. They are hermaphrodite or unisexual. Reproduction takes place asexually and sexually both. 18. Asexual reproduction takes place by budding, fragmentation and regeneration. 19. Sexual reproduction occurs by fusion of gametes. Fertilization is external. Development is indirect with a free-swimming ciliated planula larva.

Unique features First tissue graded animals, diploblastic, presence of nematocysts (stinging cells), internal hollow cavity is coelenteron, incomplete alimentary canal, polymorphism, carnivorous, coral forming animals, larva is planula Classification Phylum coelenterata is classified into three classes on the basis of composition of mesogloea and body forms.
Class 1: Hydrozoa i. Most of them are found in marine water and some of them in freshwater. ii. They occur as either polyp form (Hydra) or both polyp and medusa form (Obelia).

Mostly, they exhibit alternation of generation. iii. There is non-cellular mesogloea in between ectoderm and endoderm. iv. Few of them contribute to the formation of coral reef. v. They are colonial or solitary and free swimming or sessile forms.
Example: Hydra (freshwater polyp), Obelia (sea fur), Physalia (portages man of war), Porpita, Tubularia etc.
Class 2: Scyphozoa i. They are all solitary forms and found exclusively in marine water.

ii. Polyp stage is absent or reduced and medusa stage is dominant. Some of them exhibit alternation of generation. iii. Medusae are large bell or umbrella shaped and free swimming with marginal tentacles. iv. Gelatinous mesogloea contains amoeboid cells. v. They don’t form corals.

Example: Aurelia (jelly fish), Pericolpa, Lucernaria, Rhizostoma Class 3: Anthozoa i. They are both solitary or colonial forms and all found in marine water. ii. There is only polyp stage but no medusa stage and hence alternation of generation is absent. iii. Mesogloea is well developed that contains amoeboid cells and fibres. iv. Gastrovascular cavity is further divided by septa or mesentaries. v. They have major role in the formation of coral reef.
Example: Tubipora (organ pipe coral), Alcyonium (soft coral), heliopora (blue coral), Gorgonia (Sea fan), Metridium (sea anemone) etc.
8.2.4 PHYLUM PLATYHELMINTHES

The word platyhelminthes (Gr; platys-flat; helminthes-worms) was first proposed by Gegenbaur for flatworms. Their body is compressed dorsoventally and show bilateral symmetry. They are the first animals which have developed organ system.

General characters
1. They are mostly parasitic, living inside the organs such as liver, intestine, blood etc. of animals. Few of them are free living or commensal found in freshwater sea and moist places.
2. Their body is bilaterally symmetrical and dorso-ventrally flattened. Ventral surface bears mouth and genital openings.

3. They have organ-system grade of body organization. 4. Body is vermiform (worm like), elongated ribbon or leaf like. 5. They are microscopic or small to moderate sized and some are long ribbon measuring

13 metre length in average. 6. They are first triploblastic animals i.e. body is developed from three germ layers. 7. Body is covered with syncytial and ciliated epidermis in free living forms but parasitic forms have cuticle as outer layer and without epidermis.

8. Muscular layer of mesodermal origin lies below epidermis that consists of longitudinal, circular and oblique muscles.
